about: Quiz of the Rerankers lesson. a = index of the right option (0-based). Answer key: B A C B (as letters).

questions.q: Why can a cross-encoder notice that a passage answers this question, while a bi-encoder may only see a shared topic?
o: It reads the question and the passage together, so every question word can attend to every passage word.
It was trained on more data.
questions.f: The bi-encoder makes one vector per text before the two texts meet. The cross-encoder reads the pair as one input.

questions.q: On Q3 (the paraphrase), the answer chunk is 33rd in the bge-m3 list. The reranker scores only the top 20. What happens?
o: The answer chunk stays out: the reranker can only reorder what the first stage gave it.
The reranker finds it anyway, because it reads the whole corpus.
The first stage moves it up.
questions.f: A reranker orders a short list. It cannot promote a chunk that is not in the list. Try depth 50 in the Touch section.

questions.q: The model card reports MIRACL Persian 57.7 → 62.49 for bge-reranker-v2-m3. What is the right way to read it?
o: It proves the model is best on our Persian lectures.
It is a peer-reviewed result from the BGE M3 paper.
It is a vendor number on Wikipedia text, after one first stage; it does not test lecture text.
It shows the reranker always helps.
questions.f: The numbers come only from the card. MIRACL is Wikipedia. The Qwen3 card shows a case where this reranker made the order worse (MTEB-R 61.82 → 57.03).

questions.q: Where does our pipeline use the reranker score?
o: Only in the older chat path.
In the R list (top 10 of the fused list), in the graph list (order inside each hop group) and in the G1 abstention gate.
Only to build the index offline.
questions.f: Three places: rerank_top = 10 in R, rank rule 7 inside each hop group of the graph list, and the highest packed score for the G1 gate.
